title: [News] AI Chip Testing Capacity Tightness Prompts Customers to Lock In 1-Year-Plus Deals; Sigurd Hikes Prices
source_used: TrendForce (citing STAR Market Daily and others)
key_facts: According to STAR Market Daily, Sigurd Microelectronics (a chip testing provider, known as an OSAT) has posted monthly revenue above NT$2 billion for three consecutive months.
Most customers have signed capacity agreements lasting more than a year; some memory customers pay premiums to lock in capacity.
Sigurd confirmed it has begun raising its own prices, but said it could not speak for the industry.
AI, CPU, GPU, ASIC and silicon photonics revenue reached about NT$3.7 billion in the first nine months of 2026, up from about NT$2.5 billion a year earlier.
Sigurd raised its 2026 capex to NT$8.8 billion, 48 percent above its original plan.
According to Nomura Securities, cited by Seoul Economic Daily, Nvidia Blackwell's final test time is estimated at four times Hopper's, and Rubin could need seven times as long.
According to ETNews, Digital Frontier and UniTest secured a combined KRW 283.94 billion in HBM4 wafer tester orders from SK hynix this year.
quote_evidence: Most have signed capacity agreements lasting more than a year, while others have reserved capacity through dedicated equipment.
Asked about pricing, Sigurd said it could not speak for the industry but confirmed that it has already begun raising its own prices.
According to Seoul Economic Daily, citing Nomura Securities, NVIDIA Blackwell’s final test time is estimated to be four times that of Hopper, while Rubin could require seven times as long.
why_it_matters_hint: Testing is becoming a tighter bottleneck and cost for AI chips, and buyers are locking in capacity a year ahead.
event_date: 8 Oct 2026 (report date); underlying dates not stated
